content: Pneumococcal disease is an illness caused by the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae, commonly referred to as pneumococcus. This bacterium can be transmitted from one person to another through respiratory droplets, such as those produced when an infected individual coughs or sneezes. Pneumococcus can infect various parts of the body, leading to different types of infections, including: Pneumonia: Infection of the lungs. Otitis media: Infection of the middle ear. Sinusitis: Infection of the sinuses. Meningitis: Infection of the protective membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord. Bacteremia: Infection of the bloodstream. The symptoms of pneumococcal disease vary depending on the site of infection. Common symptoms include fever, cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, stiff neck, confusion, sensitivity to light, joint pain, chills, ear pain, difficulty sleeping, and irritability. In severe cases, the disease can result in complications such as hearing loss, brain damage, or even death. A comprehensive list of symptoms specific to each type of infection can be found on the CDC’s website. Pneumococcal disease is a global health concern but is more prevalent in lowand middle-income countries where vaccination rates are lower. In regions with four distinct seasons, the disease is more commonly observed during the winter and early spring months. In tropical areas with alternating dry and rainy seasons, pneumococcal disease tends to occur more frequently during the dry season. Vaccination is the most effective method of preventing pneumococcal disease. In the United States, pneumococcal vaccines are routinely recommended. The CDC advises the use of PCV13 or PCV15 for: All children under the age of 5. Children aged 2 to 18 years who have specific medical conditions. For individuals who have not previously received a pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, the CDC recommends PCV15 or PCV20 for: Adults aged 65 years or older. Adults aged 19 to 64 years who have certain medical conditions or other risk factors. Additionally, the CDC recommends PPSV23 for: Children aged 2 to 18 years with certain medical conditions. Adults aged 19 years or older who have already received PCV15. Certain individuals may require multiple doses or booster shots depending on their specific health circumstances. It is important to consult with a healthcare provider to determine the most appropriate vaccination schedule for you or your child.
